correctness.rationale: With \(q/p=[c_0;\ldots,c_m]\), the standard matrix product gives \(pu-qv=(-1)^m\) and hence \(a\equiv u+m\pmod2\). Modulo \(2\), even quotient matrices are transpositions and odd quotient matrices are three-cycles on the three nonzero vectors of \(\mathbb F_2^2\); because the final first column is \((1,1)^T\), this forces \(u\equiv m+o_0\pmod2\), where \(o_0\) counts odd quotients. Thus \(a\equiv\sum_i c_i\pmod2\). Renshaw's inclusion-exclusion counts then give the stated \(T(p^e q^f)\) branch. The packaged exact checker corroborates 15169 Bézout-parity cases and 304 direct totient cases.
